chunk_map.heading: You steer the answer by loading context
The loop is what you repeat

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a referent that doesn't resolve strands a reader mid-slide. Closest candidate to a violation, chunk 3 (lines 17-21): line 21 'The fix happens once. The loop is what you repeat' — 'The fix' points back at 'Fix one trivial bug from your own backlog, end-to-end' at line 19, same chunk; 'The loop' is the chunk's own header (line 17). Both resolve inside the chunk, so this stays inside the rule. Chunk 1 (lines 3-9): line 7 'Same words, different session. In the other session' resolves against 'Two Claude Code sessions' named two sentences earlier in the same chunk (line 5). Chunk 2 (lines 11-15): line 13 'Context is whatever you tell it' — 'it' = Claude, named in chunk 1 ('Claude answers Rome', line 5), carried forward as prior context per the sequential-read test. No never-named, vague, or re-chunk-stranded referent anywhere in the body. PASS.

Harm: a callback to another file by position stops resolving once deck start position shifts. Scanned all 3 body chunks (lines 1-22): no reference to another lecture, module, or document by name or position — consistent with the maintainer block's own 'Zero map references. M1 is protected.' N/A, no cross-file callback present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a backward 'the X you did/saw' pointing at a dead beat strands the reader. This file is the M1 opener (registry-confirmed: curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md:42 includes it via a plain include-link, and the maintainer block states 'Placement: M1 opener, after Connections, before the exercise') — there is no prior module beat available to reference, and body carries no 'you did/saw' construction anywhere. N/A.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reveal narrated before its guess kills the demo's payoff in delivery. Chunk 1 (lines 3-9): guess prompt at line 7 ('Take a guess before it runs. What does Claude suggest now?') precedes the reveal at line 9 ('Something Finnish: salmon, rye bread, meatballs.'). Matches the maintainer's own accept-note ('Guess before reveal. The guess paragraph precedes the Finnish-dinner answer.'). PASS.

Harm: a chunk with no self-carrying claim projects as a slide that says nothing standalone. Chunk 1 (3-9) carries the full demo-plus-reveal; chunk 2 (11-15) carries the steering claim plus its restatement ('The move is loading the right context before the question...'); chunk 3 (17-21) carries the fix-vs-loop distinction plus the payoff line. All three read as complete on their own. PASS.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a skimming reader. 'Context is King' (chunk 1) is delivered exactly: the same second question gets two different answers, attributed to what came before. 'You steer the answer by loading context' (chunk 2) is restated almost verbatim at line 15 ('The move is loading the right context before the question'). 'The loop is what you repeat' (chunk 3) is restated near-verbatim at line 21. All three headers are true summaries of their chunks. PASS.

Harm: a cadence tic reads as authorial clutter on a projected slide. Checked all six sub-patterns across all 3 chunks: (1) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' triple — none; a loose regex (grep -inE '\bNot [A-Za-z].*\. Not [A-Za-z].*\.') flags line 21 but on inspection the two 'not's are 'not one bug closed' (mid-sentence, lowercase) and a separate sentence two clauses later ('Not by reading about it.') — not an adjacent chained triple, false positive on manual read. (2) anaphora/epistrophe triples — none. (3) self-grading superlatives — grep -inE '\bone of the (most|best)\b' → 0 hits. (4) number + own retraction — no bare numeric claims in body prose (grep -noE '[0-9]+' only matches the body-view's own line-number column, not body text). (5) abstraction-noun stacks — body stays concrete throughout (pasta, osso buco, risotto; salmon, rye bread, meatballs; a rules file). (6) verb triplets with an empty leg — none. PASS on all sub-items.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: content present in long-read but absent from the composed deck silently strands a reader who toggled to Slides. File is included from a module via a plain include-link (curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md:42: '[The wizard move](lectures/the-wizard-move.md)'), the standard shape that reaches the deck. Ran node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/the-wizard-move.md → 'files: 1  slides: 3' — matches the 3 '##' chunks read from source; no phase-less prose section (no prework/supplementary block) exists in this file that could be dropped. PASS.

Ran node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/lectures/the-wizard-move.md → exact output: 'OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' PASS.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a label-shaped header on a lecture wastes the beat where a law should be named instead. This file is a lecture, so headings owe claims: 'Context is King' (a maxim), 'You steer the answer by loading context' (a claim about the reader's agency), 'The loop is what you repeat' (a definitional claim) — all three are claims, none a bare label. PASS.
